narrative.overview:
This is printed matter that happens to be running in a browser. Warm off-white stock, ink that was never quite black, hairline rules that look ruled rather than drawn, and a monospaced apparatus doing all the labelling — counts, tags, indices, field names. Against that apparatus, one high-contrast serif carries the entry titles, and the difference between the two voices is the whole typographic idea: the serif names things, the mono measures them.

The density is deliberate and slightly higher than comfortable. This is an index, not a moodboard — it should feel like a working document that has been set properly, not a gallery that has been art-directed. Every number on the page is real and recomputes: the chip counts, the NN / TT index, the tag overflow. Nothing is decorative typography pretending to be data.

Color is almost entirely absent from the chrome, because the chrome is competing with screenshots that each arrive with their own palette and will always win. The single exception is the group ink system: each design group owns one saturated printing ink, and that ink is the only chroma the interface itself is permitted. It does structural work — identifying a group at a glance across the whole grid — and it never decorates.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground, never white, never cream-sweet
Zero border radius anywhere; printed matter has cut edges
Monospace for all apparatus, high-contrast serif for all names
Flat by default: depth comes from border weight and tonal layering, not shadow
One saturated ink per group, used structurally and sparingly

rules.name: The Screenshot Owns The Color Rule
rules.body: Saturated color in the chrome is reserved for group inks. Everything else is paper, ink, soft ink, and rule. If a new UI element needs a color to be understood, it needs better typography instead.

rules.name: The Warm Neutral Rule
rules.body: No neutral in this system is chromatically neutral. Every grey and every black carries a yellow-red cast. A cool grey anywhere on the page is a bug.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: The serif names, the mono measures. A title is never mono; a count, tag, label, or index is never serif. There is no third typeface.

rules.name: The Brief Is Prose Rule
rules.body: Every input in the library is a field and is set in mono. The studio’s brief is the one exception: it is a sentence a person writes, not a value they enter, so it is set in the serif. Nothing else that accepts typing may be.

rules.name: The Tabular Figure Rule
rules.body: Every number in the interface uses font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. Counts and indices change constantly as filters apply, and columns must not jitter.

rules.name: The Flat Page Rule
rules.body: If an element needs a shadow to be legible, its border weight is wrong. Hover states change border color and tonal value, never elevation.

dos: Do keep border radius at 0 on every element, without exception.
Do give every group exactly one ink and reuse it in all three sanctioned places.
Do use tabular-nums on every number that can change.
Do express hover as a border-color and tonal change only.
Do let the screenshot bleed to the card’s edge; the image is the content, the caption is the apparatus.
Do keep the chip bar fully visible and wrapping, never horizontally scrolling.
donts: Don’t introduce a sans-serif. The system has exactly two faces.
Don’t add a shadow to any element except the detail overlay.
Don’t use pure white (#FFF) or pure black (#000) anywhere.
Don’t use a chromatically neutral grey; every neutral carries a warm cast.
Don’t let group ink touch body text, borders, or backgrounds outside the three sanctioned uses.
Don’t replace the grid with masonry; equal-height rows exist so treatments can be compared across a row.
Don’t show copy confirmation as a toast or floating notification.
